4. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.239 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Trans Yamuna, District Agra, during the pendency of trial.

entities.text: Police Station Trans Yamuna, District Agra
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is the mother-in-law of the deceased and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
She has nothing to do with the said offence.
There are general and omnibus allegations against all the accused persons including the applicant.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that the cause of death is asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem hanging.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 18.06.2024 and her fundamental rights enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India stand violated.
The applicant is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, she will not misuse the liberty of bail.

7. Learnedcounsel for the informant and learned State Law Officerhave vehemently opposed the bail application and have fairly stated that no witness has been examined till date and even no witness was present till 15.07.2025.

8.The Supreme Court in the case of Union of India vs. K.A. Najeeb, AIR 2021 SC 712, has observed as under:-
"We are conscious of the fact that the charges levelled against the respondent are grave and a serious threat to societal harmony.

entities.text: Union of India vs. K.A. Najeeb, AIR 2021 SC 712
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Had it been a case at the threshold,
we would have outrightly turned down the respondent's prayer.

However, keeping in mind the length of the period spent by him in custody and the unlikelihood of the trial being completed anytime soon, the High Court appears to have been left with no other option except to grant bail."

9. The Supreme Court in the judgment ofKahkashan Kausar @ Sonam vs. The State of Bihar, (2022)
6 SCC 599has categorically opined that the Courts should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

entities.text:
ofKahkashan Kausar @ Sonam vs. The State of Bihar, (2022)
6 SCC 599has
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out.

10. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, taking into consideration the fact that the applicant is the mother-in-law of the deceased person and no witness has been examined to date, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant-Smt. Shahnaz, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.

sentences.text: (i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence during trial.
(ii) The applicant shall not pressurise/intimidate with the prosecution witnesses.
(iii) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed.
12. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

13. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
